aciR: Assimilative Causal Inference for Conditional Gaussian Nonlinear Systems

Source: R/aciR-package.R
aciR-package.Rd

The aciR package implements assimilative causal inference (ACI) for conditional Gaussian nonlinear systems (CGNS). A CGNS pairs an observed signal with an unobserved component whose conditional statistics, given the observed path, are Gaussian and available in closed form.

Details

Most analyses need three calls. aci_dyad_model() or aci_cgns_model() builds an aci_model, aci_simulate() draws a realisation of it, and aci() runs the whole workflow on an observed signal and returns an aci object with summary.aci(), plot.aci() and as.data.frame.aci() methods.

Beneath that sits the numerical core, comprising the forward filter (aci_filter()), the backward smoother (aci_smoother()) and the relative-entropy causal-information metric (aci_metric()). The three are written against a general CGNS components list rather than a specific model, so they apply to any conditional Gaussian system. aci_components documents that schema and aci_dyad_components() is its worked example.

The numerical core is graded against fixtures generated by an independent MATLAB harness reproducing the deterministic core of the reference implementation. The Validation and the independent oracle vignette records the design, the provenance and the observed agreement; the Assumptions and interpretation vignette states what the method assumes and what an ACI peak does and does not support.

The method reimplemented here is due to Andreou, Chen and Bollt (2026).

References

Andreou, M., Chen, N. and Bollt, E. (2026). Assimilative causal inference. Nature Communications, 17, 1854. doi:10.1038/s41467-026-68568-0
